selectedProblem: Native child IPC read an input ACK header and suffix directly from raw stdout even though the outer service client already buffers ACKs.
change: Create one bounded 128-byte reader in crashguard.NewClient, then route Process.ExchangeInput through the same client reader. Guard ledger and native input retain prefetched bytes across exchanges.

quantitative.fixture: 48 contiguous ACK bytes decoded as a 24-byte header plus 24-byte suffix
quantitative.complexity: Time O(n) in bytes remains unchanged; additional buffer memory O(1) per process, not per frame.

validation.red: Both new regressions failed on unmodified production code with 2 and 3 underlying Reads respectively.
validation.green: crashguard and inputworker full package suites passed; their vet checks passed.
validation.race: Targeted crashguard shared-reader and real portable input/cursor/guard IPC tests passed under -race

limits: The fixture counts underlying io.Reader calls under complete-contiguous-delivery conditions. Fragmented delivery may require more reads.
This is not a measured 50 percent end-to-end latency improvement or proof that the full 111.619ms delay came from ACK reads.
APIChanges: none; wire formats and public signatures unchanged
